procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months out from the hysterectomy and the ureter repair stent.
Stent came out 11/20 at urology, ultrasound beforehand without hydronephrosis per her. No flank pain since, urine clear, no infections. Incision healed. Back to full teaching days.
Saw pulmonology on 1/8 and repeated her breathing tests: told they were about the same as last summer and to stay on prednisone 10. Still some breathlessness on the stairs, no worse. Dry cough comes and goes.
Has the hydrocortisone kits, one at home and one in the nurse's office at school. Has not needed one. No illnesses this winter.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, incision well healed. No CVA tenderness.

A/P
1. Ureteral injury, healed after stenting. Resolved.
2. Sarcoidosis, stable per pulm, prednisone 10 daily.
3. Adrenal insufficiency: sick-day plan in place, kits current.
4. Osteopenia: alendronate, calcium/D.
Physical in the spring.

documents.title: Letter for school nurse
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Our school nurse asked for a doctor's note about the emergency hydrocortisone kit I keep in her office, saying what it's for and when it should be used. Can you write one?

documents.title: Letter to school nurse
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To the school nurse: Ms. Aisha Owusu is under my care for adrenal insufficiency related to long-term steroid treatment. She keeps an emergency hydrocortisone 100 mg intramuscular kit at school. It should be given into the outer thigh if she is vomiting and unable to keep her medication down, is confused or very drowsy, or collapses, and 911 should be called right away even if it is given. She is trained to self-inject. Please contact our office with questions. Primary care physician.

documents.title: Refills: alendronate, calcium/vitamin D
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail order renewals for alendronate 70 mg weekly and calcium carbonate/D3 600/400 BID. Both on active list. Sent with refills to cover until her April physical and beyond.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 44F.
Missed last fall's mammogram while recovering, wants to catch up. Feeling well. Stairs still make her breathless at the top, unchanged since winter. Cough occasional. No flank pain or urinary symptoms. No illness requiring extra steroid since the surgery. Eye check due this summer.
Meds: prednisone 10 daily; calcium/D3 600/400 BID; alendronate 70 weekly; hydrocortisone 100 mg IM emergency kit. NKDA.
Social: teaching, finishing the year. Never smoker. Rare wine.
ROS: no fevers, sweats or weight change. No vision changes or eye pain. No joint pain. No bowel change.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Eyes white, no redness. No cervical or axillary nodes. Lungs clear without crackles. Heart regular, no murmur. Breasts without masses or skin change. Abdomen soft, healed midline scar. Skin without rash. No edema.

A/P
1. Sarcoidosis, lung Stage II with prior uveitis and skin findings: stable on prednisone 10 per pulm.
2. Adrenal insufficiency, steroid-related, with crisis in 2025: sick-day plan reviewed, kits not expired.
3. Osteopenia on steroids: alendronate, calcium/D; vitamin D today.
4. Steroid labs: CMP, A1c, lipids, CBC.
5. Prevention: mammogram ordered. No cervical screening after hysterectomy for benign disease. Colon screening starts at 45 this fall. PHQ-2 negative. Flu and COVID at the fall visit.
RTC October.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs are all normal: blood sugar and A1c, kidney and liver function, blood count, cholesterol, vitamin D. No changes. Radiology should call about the mammogram.

reports.text: Bilateral screening tomosynthesis. Prior studies 2023 and 2024 for comparison. Heterogeneously dense breasts. No suspicious masses, calcifications or areas of distortion. No change from prior.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Visit Note
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Outside ophthalmology. Exam date 06/09/2026. Routine surveillance, history of sarcoid anterior uveitis, on systemic prednisone. Vision stable. Slit lamp: anterior chambers deep and quiet both eyes, no cells or flare, no keratic precipitates, lenses clear. Intraocular pressure normal both eyes. Impression: no active uveitis. Return in one year or sooner for redness, pain or blurring.

documents.title: Refill: prednisone
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail order request, prednisone 10 mg daily. 90 days with 3 refills sent.

documents.title: Fall appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I want to get my October visit on the books before school starts and my schedule fills up. Late afternoon if possible. Can I get my flu shot at it too?

documents.title: RE: Fall appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked Tuesday 10/13 at 3:30. Yes, we can give the flu shot then.
